quests.instruction: Fill in the blank with the correct word.
quests.passage: The company launched three new products last quarter. ____ of them, however, sold as well as expected.
quests.hint: This word shows that not even one succeeded, referring back to 'three.'
quests.explanation: 'None' correctly refers to zero out of the three products mentioned, unlike 'both' (for two) or 'every.'

quests.instruction: Choose the word that best completes the passage.
quests.passage: Interest rates rose sharply this year, and ____ has made borrowing far more expensive for homeowners.
quests.hint: This word refers back to the whole idea of rates rising, not a single noun.
quests.explanation: 'This' refers to the entire preceding idea (the rate rise), which 'it' alone cannot capture as clearly.

quests.instruction: Select the option that fits the context.
quests.passage: The team tried two strategies to boost sales. The first was a discount campaign; the ____ involved social media ads.
quests.hint: This word signals the second item in an ordered list of two.
quests.explanation: 'The second' correctly continues the ordered pair started by 'the first.'

quests.instruction: Choose the word that best completes the passage.
quests.passage: The factory reduced its emissions by installing new filters. ____ change also lowered its energy costs.
quests.hint: This word refers back to the entire action just described, functioning as a determiner before 'change.'
quests.explanation: 'This change' refers back to installing filters, treating the whole action as a single noun phrase.

quests.instruction: Select the option that fits the context.
quests.passage: Some readers found the ending satisfying, while ____ felt it was too abrupt.
quests.hint: This word contrasts with 'some' to describe a different group of people.
quests.explanation: 'Others' pairs naturally with 'some' when describing two groups within a larger set.

quests.instruction: Complete the sentence with the most suitable word.
quests.passage: The report covers three regions. In ____ case, sales grew by at least ten percent.
quests.hint: This word means 'every single one, considered individually,' and fits directly before 'case.'
quests.explanation: 'Each case' treats every region individually, fitting the singular noun 'case.'

quests.instruction: Select the option that fits the context.
quests.passage: The article doesn't explain why the policy failed; ____, it simply lists the consequences.
quests.hint: This connector shows the article does one thing rather than another.
quests.explanation: 'Instead' shows a substitution — the article lists consequences rather than explaining causes.

quests.instruction: Complete the sentence with the most suitable word.
quests.passage: The survey shows growing support for remote work; ____, many managers remain unconvinced.
quests.hint: This connector introduces a fact that seems to go against the previous statement.
quests.explanation: 'Nevertheless' introduces a contrast, showing manager doubt despite growing employee support.

quests.instruction: Choose the word that makes the passage clear and natural.
quests.passage: The proposal saves money in the short term. In the long run, ____, it could actually cost more.
quests.hint: This connector signals a contrast between short-term and long-term effects.
quests.explanation: 'However' signals contrast, matching a plan that looks good short-term but not long-term.

quests.instruction: Complete the sentence with the most suitable word.
quests.passage: The reviewer's tone throughout the piece is clearly ____; every sentence seems designed to mock the film.
quests.hint: This word describes a tone that mocks through irony.
quests.explanation: 'Sarcastic' matches a tone built around mockery, consistent with the description.

quests.instruction: Choose the word that makes the passage clear and natural.
quests.passage: Although the letter is polite in wording, its underlying message is unmistakably ____.
quests.hint: This word describes a hidden, hostile intention beneath polite language.
quests.explanation: 'Threatening' captures an intimidating undertone hidden beneath polite surface language.

quests.instruction: Pick the word that best fits the meaning of the passage.
quests.passage: The speech avoided taking a clear position on the issue, staying deliberately ____ throughout.
quests.hint: This adjective describes language that is intentionally unclear.
quests.explanation: 'Vague' fits a speech that avoids clarity, contrasting with 'blunt' or 'decisive.'

quests.instruction: Choose the word that makes the passage clear and natural.
quests.passage: The purpose of the pilot program is not to replace teachers, but ____ to support them with better tools.
quests.hint: This word pairs with 'not...but' to clarify the true purpose.
quests.explanation: 'But rather' clarifies purpose, contrasting what the program is not with what it truly is.

quests.instruction: Pick the word that best fits the meaning of the passage.
quests.passage: The bridge was built primarily ____ ease congestion on the older route, not to attract tourists.
quests.hint: This introduces the infinitive expressing the main purpose of the bridge.
quests.explanation: 'To ease' is the infinitive of purpose, correctly explaining why the bridge was built.

quests.instruction: Fill in the blank with the correct word.
quests.passage: The policy exists ____ protect consumers from misleading advertising, according to its authors.
quests.hint: This introduces the infinitive verb expressing the policy's intended purpose.
quests.explanation: 'Exists to protect' uses the infinitive of purpose, matching the stated intent of the policy.

quests.instruction: Pick the word that best fits the meaning of the passage.
quests.passage: In my opinion, the film's biggest weakness ____ its uneven pacing rather than its acting.
quests.hint: This phrase means 'is located in' or 'can be found in.'
quests.explanation: 'Lies in' means is found in, matching a claim about where the film's flaw is located.

quests.instruction: Fill in the blank with the correct word.
quests.passage: Critics have long debated whether the author's later novels ____ up to his earlier, more celebrated work.
quests.hint: This verb pairs with 'up to' meaning to reach the same standard.
quests.explanation: 'Measure up to' means to reach the same standard, fitting a comparison across an author's career.

quests.instruction: Choose the word that best completes the passage.
quests.passage: It's worth noting that the study's sample size was small, which may ____ its overall conclusions.
quests.hint: This verb means to weaken the strength of something.
quests.explanation: 'Undermine' means to weaken, fitting how a small sample might reduce a study's reliability.

quests.instruction: Fill in the blank with the correct word.
quests.passage: The two proposals differ mainly in scope: one focuses on local reform, ____ the other targets national policy.
quests.hint: This word contrasts two parallel clauses describing different scopes.
quests.explanation: 'While' contrasts two parallel ideas, matching local versus national focus.

quests.instruction: Choose the word that best completes the passage.
quests.passage: The committee's decision, ____ controversial, was ultimately upheld by the board.
quests.hint: This word introduces a concession before the main clause continues.
quests.explanation: 'Though controversial' is a reduced concessive clause, meaning 'although it was controversial.'

quests.instruction: Select the option that fits the context.
quests.passage: The plan received little public attention at the time; it was only ____ hindsight that its importance became clear.
quests.hint: This preposition completes the fixed phrase meaning 'looking back afterward.'
quests.explanation: 'In hindsight' is a fixed phrase meaning looking back afterward, matching delayed recognition.

quests.instruction: Choose the word that best completes the passage.
quests.passage: The article's central ____ is that automation will reshape, not eliminate, most jobs.
quests.hint: This noun refers to a statement someone argues is true.
quests.explanation: 'Claim' refers to the main argument being made, matching the article's central idea.

quests.instruction: Select the option that fits the context.
quests.passage: Supporters of the plan point to lower costs; opponents, ____, emphasize the risk of job losses.
quests.hint: This connector introduces a contrasting viewpoint happening at the same time.
quests.explanation: 'Meanwhile' introduces a simultaneous, contrasting viewpoint from a different group.

quests.instruction: Complete the sentence with the most suitable word.
quests.passage: The evidence presented was compelling, ____ some experts still question the study's methodology.
quests.hint: This word introduces a concession that weakens the initial praise.
quests.explanation: 'Although' introduces a concession, contrasting compelling evidence with lingering doubts.

quests.instruction: Select the option that fits the context.
quests.passage: The council's new parking rules have proven ____ unpopular that a petition against them has already gathered thousands of signatures.
quests.hint: This word pairs with an adjective and 'that' to show a strong result.
quests.explanation: 'So...that' is the fixed structure linking an adjective to its dramatic result.

quests.instruction: Complete the sentence with the most suitable word.
quests.passage: It was ____ a minor error that the editor almost let it pass without correction.
quests.hint: This word pairs with a noun phrase and 'that' to show a strong result.
quests.explanation: 'Such a...that' is the fixed structure linking a noun phrase to its result.

quests.instruction: Choose the word that makes the passage clear and natural.
quests.passage: The film is not ____ bad that it's unwatchable, but it's far from memorable either.
quests.hint: This word pairs with an adjective and 'that' in a negative structure.
quests.explanation: 'Not so...that' negates a strong result, softening the criticism of the film.

quests.instruction: Complete the sentence with the most suitable word.
quests.passage: What makes the design remarkable is not its complexity, ____ its surprising simplicity.
quests.hint: This word pairs with 'not' to introduce the true, contrasting reason.
quests.explanation: 'Not...but' introduces the actual reason, replacing the rejected first option.

quests.instruction: Choose the word that makes the passage clear and natural.
quests.passage: The company's success can be attributed, at least ____, to its early investment in staff training.
quests.hint: This phrase means 'partly,' softening a claim about a single cause.
quests.explanation: 'In part' softens the claim, acknowledging training as one of several contributing factors.

quests.instruction: Pick the word that best fits the meaning of the passage.
quests.passage: Whatever the outcome of the trial, the case has already ____ raised questions about industry regulation.
quests.hint: This adverb means 'in a way that cannot be denied.'
quests.explanation: 'Undeniably' means clearly true, fitting the strong claim that questions have been raised.
